findings.location: Implementation Design, ID-I03; contracts/navigation-tool.md, Process and source protection
findings.affected_requirement: O-NFR01; spec FR-005; Constitution I and V
findings.evidence: The revised plan requires Infrastructure to resolve JDT-LS and Java from host PATH, but does not define how it rejects a candidate supplied through a prepared-source directory, tool-state directory, current-directory search or another untrusted PATH entry. Worker arguments cannot choose the command, yet the resulting process could still execute untrusted source as jdtls.bat or java.exe before navigation containment checks. The batch/interpreter child restriction is stated, but the executable selection trust boundary is unspecified.
findings.correction_outcome: Keep the user's PATH-only choice while specifying trusted PATH resolution: exclude prepared-source and disposable tool-state directories and unintended current-directory lookup, validate the selected command location/type before launch, pin the resolved executable identity for the session, and fail closed on an untrusted candidate. Apply the same approved process boundary to any batch/interpreter children and add a qualification seam for rejected candidates.

raw_result.summary: Plan-only REVISE. The PATH direction consistently replaces config-file and .env/JDT_LS_BIN selection, and deterministic implementation-design validation returned no errors. Prior raw plan verdicts 01–03 had no findings; their accepted hashes were invalidated by this later user change. P-PATH-TRUST-01 is newly introduced by the PATH executable decision. Existing 18.1/18.3 authority, restricted-profile and no-write obligations remain intact. No current tasks artifact was reviewed. diff_sha256 is SHA-256 of canonical sorted path-to-artifact-SHA256 JSON encoded as UTF-8 with a terminal newline.
